Reason: The chest X-rays (PA and lateral) show a large, well-defined opacity in the left upper hemithorax/anterior mediastinum (marked by *) that is causing contralateral (rightward) tracheal deviation. This mass effect is characteristic of a space-occupying lesion such as a tumor (e.g., pleuropulmonary synovial sarcoma), rather than a simple effusion, consolidation, or pneumothorax.
